facts.text: Gardens derives its name from the Dutch East India Company's original garden laid out in 1652 by Hendrik Boom near the Fresh River.
The suburb hosts South Africa's oldest garden, Company Gardens, a public park that once supplied food to early Cape settlers.
Kloof Street, the main thoroughfare, is famed for fashion stores, second‑hand furniture, restaurants, and art galleries that reflect the area's creative scene.
The University of Cape Town’s Fine Arts department, Michaelis School of Fine Art, sits in Gardens and was founded in 1925.
Government Avenue, also called “The Gardens”, was originally lined with lemon and orange trees and later oak trees planted by Simon van der Stel.
Gardens is home to the Iziko South African National Gallery, one of the country's premier art museums, located within the historic Company Gardens.
